The **Demon Tower** begins to break down into its component **Shadows**, which flatten into two dimensions and disappear. At the end of the current round, the **Demon Tower** will disappear completely. It will reappear at the end of the following round healed by **20 HP**. This process can be prevented if the **Demon Tower** takes 30 or more damage, or is afflicted with a new Status Effect, before the end of the current round.

KncxEFNoLo1E18slhl7m.description:
Formed from an amalgamation of countless **Shadows**, the **Demon Tower** is a terrifying and disconcerting foe. Since **Shadows** lack any active thought or strategic capability, the formation of a **Demon Tower** is not a conscious decision; it is a force of nature, like innumerable dark streams coming together to form an inexorable current.

The **Demon Tower's** strange form is difficult to combat--it is alternately malleable and unyielding. It can flow like a river, strike with the force of a hammer, or spread like a wave. When sufficiently threatened, it can temporarily *Disperse*, then re-constitute itself. Individual **Shadows** occasionally fall from its mass, suggesting some oversaturation or instability.

Since **Demon Towers** have rarely been seen outside the Dark Realm, some theorize that they can only form in the presence of large amounts of dark energy. 


*Original art by Tetsuya Nomura.*

special.effect:
All abilities that “*consume memories*” cause “**amnesia**.” When afflicted by **amnesia**, characters lose their **traits** in this order: **Origin**, **Theme**, and finally **Identity**. Losing all **traits** automatically brings characters to **0 HP**, triggering the **Surrendering** mechanic and preventing them from using the **Sacrifice** mechanic and from gaining **2 Fabula Points**. This symbolizes the complete loss of the character’s memories, meaning the character has lost all will to fight.

Because of this, unless otherwise specified, players may choose to reduce a **bond** to zero instead of losing a **trait**. However, this leads to another consequence. When a **bond** with another player character is reduced to zero, the character without that **bond** can no longer direct effects toward that other character until the other character first directs an effect at the one who has **amnesia**. This represents that the character affected by **amnesia** has lost all memories related to the other character, no longer recognizing their presence until the forgotten character makes them remember their existence.

special.effect:
Wendigo Hopper is treated **Vulnerable** to damage dealt by sources which can have **multiple targets**, but **Resistant** to damage dealt by sources which can only hit **one target**. 
But while in **Crisis** the Wendigo Hopper consumes **all of its own Mind Points** and gains **Absorption** to **all damage types**, except for **physical** and **poison**.

notes.effect:
This adversary’s goal is to deprive players of their triggers to use **Fabula Points** during combat. The idea is to create tension as their options fade away, making **Fabula Points** feel more valuable as a resource.
It’s important to note that characters can form new **bonds** during **resting scenes**, and can change their **identity** and/or **theme** when **leveling up**—both without major costs. Thus, except for **origin**, all other consequences of **amnesia** can be remedied. However, it’s recommended that the GM provide players with some way to recover their memories, since the consequences of **amnesia** have a strong impact on character roleplay and may feel overly punitive for players who invested heavily in their character’s background.

Furthermore, the **Vulnerability** and **Resistance** affinities still apply to **Physical** and **Poison** damage types, as stated in the exceptions.
Finally, this **Special Rule** is meant to consume the **Ultima Points** of the *Wendigo Hopper*, while illustrating why the swarm has not been eradicated to this day.
